newsitem.title: USA: Texas priest says parents share blame in abuse case.
newsitem.headline: Texas priest says parents share blame in abuse case.

text.p: Parents bear more responsibility than the Catholic Church for the sexual abuse of former altar boys who won a record $120 million judgment against the church last month, a priest was quoted as saying on Friday.
Monsignor Robert Rehkemper told the Dallas Morning News that the victims knew what they were doing when they submitted to the sexual advances of priest Rudolph Kos.

"No one ever says anything about what the role of the parents was in all this," said Rehkemper, who was the second-ranking official in the diocese when the abuse occurred during an 11-year period ending in 1992.
"They more properly should have known because they're close to the kids," he said.
"Parents have the prime responsibility to look after their kids. I don't want to judge them one way or the other, but it doesn't appear they were very concerned about their kids," Rehkemper said.

Of the 11 victims who sued the church, Rehkemper said, "They knew what was right and what was wrong... Anybody who reaches the age of reason shares responsibility for what they do." The plaintiffs now range in age from 18 to the early 30s.

Kos, who was suspended from the priesthood in 1992, was accused of abusing boys as young as 9 years old on hundreds of occasions at three Dallas-area churches. The victims said he had sleepovers in his rectory room where he gave them candy and video games and plied them with sedatives, alcohol and marijuana.
Rehkemper, 73, said he regretted what happened to the boys and prayed for them every day. He resigned his diocese post in 1992 and now leads a Dallas church.

During the 11-week trial, which ended July 24 with the $120 million judgment -- the largest ever against the church in a sexual abuse case -- plaintiffs attorneys said Rehkemper did not do enough to stop Kos, despite growing suspicions about his activities.
"I acted as responsibly as I could. I couldn't hide under his bed," he told the newspaper.
Gail Pawlik, mother of one of the victims, said Rehkemper was wrong to blame the parents.
"I refuse to feel guilty. I have done absolutely nothing wrong. What safer place could there be than to make sure your kids are with a priest?" she said.
Monsignor John Bell, judicial vicar and chancellor for the Dallas diocese, said Rehkemper's views did not reflect those of the church.
"He wasn't speaking for the diocese, that's for sure," he said.
Bishop Charles Grahmann, who heads the Dallas diocese, apologised to the victims in a July 27 mass.
